Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Sections 19.1, 19.3 and the 19.4 remedy (re-performance, repair, replacement, then refund) and the 19.5 disclaimer carve-out are all sound and do not swallow the express warranties. The material failure is Section 19.2: a fifteen-day conformance period running from delivery, with an express statement that Vendor has no correction or refund obligation thereafter, falls below even the fallback of 90 days for software / 30 days for services. It is also shorter than the fifteen-business-day acceptance testing window in Section 6.1, so the warranty can lapse before Customer has finished testing, and the cut-off risks neutralising the Section 19.4 remedy for the general conformance warranty in 19.1. Redline extends the period to ninety days from acceptance and deletes the cut-off, preserving the existing 19.4 remedy.

Original paragraphs:
p0076: 19.2 For fifteen days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation; after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation.

Resolved definitions:
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Meridian Fieldworks, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Copperleaf Technology Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Deliverable: 1.4 “Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.

Rendered redline:
p0076: 19.2 For ninety days after acceptance, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and the specifications in the applicable Order Form, and Vendor will correct any nonconformity reported during that period in accordance with Section 19.4.

Comment:
[Playbook] We extended the Deliverable conformance warranty to ninety days running from acceptance and removed the language cutting off Vendor's correction and refund obligation, since a fifteen-day period expires before the fifteen-business-day acceptance window in Section 6.1 even closes. Our playbook position is 12 months for software and 90 days for deliverables/services with repair, replacement or refund; we can discuss a shorter period if it still runs from acceptance and preserves the Section 19.4 remedy.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum-fee-on-termination payable by Customer appears anywhere: searches for "liquidated damages", "termination fee", "early termination", acceleration and shortfall language return nothing directed at Customer. Termination for convenience under § 9.4 requires Customer to pay only for conforming Services delivered through the termination date with a refund of prepaid Fees, and both § 9.4 and § 27.3 confirm termination is "without penalty"; § 7.3 further bars interest on amounts found not due. The only Customer-payable amounts found (§ 22.2 audit shortfall and costs following a >5% underpayment) are compensatory true-ups, not liquidated damages. ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Meridian Fieldworks, Inc.; counterparty is Copperleaf Technology Ltd..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

reasons: Deviation classification is correct: a fifteen-day conformance window falls below even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services), and the express 'no correction or refund obligation thereafter' language undercuts the Section 19.4 remedy, so this is a material failure of the fallback rather than a mere shortfall from preferred wording.

The redline reaches the playbook position: period extended to ninety days, the cut-off sentence deleted, and the existing Section 19.4 remedy (re-performance, repair, replacement, refund) expressly preserved by cross-reference rather than duplicated — a proportionate rewrite of a single short clause.

The failed deterministic period check is a phrasing artifact ('ninety days' spelled out rather than '90 days'); the 0.602 changed-character ratio is justified because the clause had to be rewritten to remove the obligation cut-off, and the rest of Section 19 (19.1, 19.3, 19.4, 19.5 carve-out) was correctly left untouched.

Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, cites the playbook position and offers a workable fallback (shorter period if it runs from acceptance and preserves the 19.4 remedy); the Section 6.1 acceptance-window point is a legitimate supporting argument.

Minor note for the drafter: adding conformance to 'the specifications in the applicable Order Form' goes slightly beyond the rule's documentation-conformance scope and beyond the minimum edit needed; it is a small, defensible improvement but could be dropped if the counterparty pushes back, and shifting the trigger from delivery to acceptance should be flagged as a negotiable point.

reasons: Status is 'compliant' and, as expected for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment was produced — the rendered paragraphs are identical to the originals.

The cited text supports the preferred position: § 9.4 limits Customer's exposure on convenience termination to Fees for conforming Services delivered plus a refund of prepaid Fees; § 27.3 confirms force-majeure termination is 'without penalty'; § 7.3 bars interest on amounts found not due. No liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum-fee-on-termination payable by Customer appears in the cited material.

The take-or-pay commitment in § 2.1 is correctly identified as the nearest economic analogue but is a minimum-volume obligation properly handled under the dedicated minimum-commitment rule; the playbook's no-double-flag instruction supports not raising it again here, and the rationale flags it transparently rather than hiding it.

Rationale accurately notes that the audit shortfall/true-up amounts are compensatory rather than liquidated damages, so they do not trigger the rule (which applies only when Customer pays an LD or penalty).

input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 imposes a multi-year (three-year) USD 2,000,000 per annum take-or-pay commitment on us expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — squarely the rule's walk-away position and well short of the fallback (single 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up rather than penalty). It also conflicts with § 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment), § 7.1 (no undisclosed minimum-use charge) and § 9.4 (Customer's 30-day convenience termination with refund of prepaid Fees), so the surrounding bargain is a no-minimum deal and the preferred position is proportionate. Redline replaces the take-or-pay with pay-for-what-is-used-or-ordered language, with the 12-month/true-up fallback offered in the comment.

proposal.summary: Remove three-year take-or-pay minimum and pay only for Services ordered or used
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment: our playbook does not accept minimum purchase commitments, and a multi-year commitment with no reduction or termination right also conflicts with the no-minimum-volume acknowledgement in § 12.3 and the convenience right in § 9.4. If a commitment is commercially necessary, we can discuss one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and settled by true-up rather than penalty.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Meridian Fieldworks, Inc.; counterparty is Copperleaf Technology Ltd..

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Meridian Fieldworks, Inc.; counterparty is Copperleaf Technology Ltd..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

**Finding: deviation (§ 2.1, p0012)** — redline validated and submitted.

- **Issue:** § 2.1 binds us to a three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" — the rule's walk-away scenario, and materially worse than the fallback (12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up not penalty).
- **Internal conflict supporting removal:** § 12.3 has Vendor acknowledge we made *no* minimum-volume commitment, § 7.1 bars undisclosed minimum-use charges, and § 9.4 gives us 30-day convenience termination with refund of prepaid Fees — so the rest of the bargain is a no-minimum deal, making the preferred position proportionate.
- **Edit:** replaced the commitment with "Customer has no minimum purchase commitment. Customer will pay only for Services used or ordered during the applicable term," consistent with precedent seed-mincommit, and the 12-month/true-up fallback is offered in the comment.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 2.1 imposes a multi-year (three-year) USD 2,000,000 per annum take-or-pay commitment on us expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — squarely the rule's walk-away position and well short of the fallback (single 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up rather than penalty). It also conflicts with § 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment), § 7.1 (no undisclosed minimum-use charge) and § 9.4 (Customer's 30-day convenience termination with refund of prepaid Fees), so the surrounding bargain is a no-minimum deal and the preferred position is proportionate. Redline replaces the take-or-pay with pay-for-what-is-used-or-ordered language, with the 12-month/true-up fallback offered in the comment.

Original paragraphs:
p0012: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Meridian Fieldworks, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Copperleaf Technology Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Services: 1.7 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.

Rendered redline:
p0012: 2.1 Customer has no minimum purchase commitment. Customer will pay only for Services used or ordered during the applicable term.

Comment:
[Playbook] We removed the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment: our playbook does not accept minimum purchase commitments, and a multi-year commitment with no reduction or termination right also conflicts with the no-minimum-volume acknowledgement in § 12.3 and the convenience right in § 9.4. If a commitment is commercially necessary, we can discuss one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and settled by true-up rather than penalty.

input.quote: 11.1 Immediately on termination Vendor shall discontinue all assistance and permanently delete Customer Data without offering an export or migration support.
input.rationale: Section 11.1 is walk-away territory: it requires immediate cessation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data with no export or migration support, so there is no transition assistance period at all (not even the 90-day fallback). It also contradicts Sections 11.2 (30-day return in a machine-readable format) and 11.3 (deletion only after confirmed return, with officer certification), and the "agreed transition period" contemplated by Section 10.1. Sections 11.2-11.3 already satisfy the preferred data-return and certified-deletion elements, so the minimal fix is to replace 11.1 with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates and subordinate deletion to 11.2-11.3.

Sections 11.2-11.3 already satisfy the preferred data-return and certified-deletion elements, so the minimal fix is to replace 11.1 with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates and subordinate deletion to 11.2-11.3.

proposal.summary: Replace immediate-deletion/no-assistance clause in 11.1 with up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, aligned with the data return and deletion mechanics in 11.2-11.3.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced the immediate cessation of assistance and deletion of Customer Data with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, which our playbook requires and which is also needed for the export and certified-deletion mechanics in Sections 11.2 and 11.3 and the transition period referenced in Section 10.1 to work. If six months is difficult, we can accept ninety days.

ops.oldText: Immediately on termination Vendor shall discontinue all assistance and permanently delete Customer Data without offering an export or migration support.
ops.newText: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or an Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance, including export and migration support, for up to six months after the effective date of expiry or termination at Vendor's then-current rates. Vendor shall not delete Customer Data except in accordance with Sections 11.2 and 11.3.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.

Parties: we represent Meridian Fieldworks, Inc.; counterparty is Copperleaf Technology Ltd..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

**Finding submitted: deviation (Section 11.1, ¶p0045).**

- **Issue:** § 11.1 mandates immediate discontinuation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data with no export or migration support — squarely in the playbook's walk-away territory, and short of even the 90-day fallback.
- **Internal conflict:** It contradicts § 11.2 (30-day return in a commonly used, machine-readable format), § 11.3 (deletion only after Customer confirms return, with officer certification), and the "agreed transition period" referenced in § 10.1.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** § 11.1 replaced with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, including export and migration support, and deletion subordinated to §§ 11.2–11.3. Because 11.2–11.3 already deliver the preferred return and certified-deletion mechanics, this single paragraph swap is the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; the comment offers 90 days as a fallback.

Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 11.1 is walk-away territory: it requires immediate cessation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data with no export or migration support, so there is no transition assistance period at all (not even the 90-day fallback). It also contradicts Sections 11.2 (30-day return in a machine-readable format) and 11.3 (deletion only after confirmed return, with officer certification), and the "agreed transition period" contemplated by Section 10.1. Sections 11.2-11.3 already satisfy the preferred data-return and certified-deletion elements, so the minimal fix is to replace 11.1 with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates and subordinate deletion to 11.2-11.3.

Original paragraphs:
p0045: 11.1 Immediately on termination Vendor shall discontinue all assistance and permanently delete Customer Data without offering an export or migration support.

Resolved definitions:

Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Meridian Fieldworks, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Copperleaf Technology Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Customer Data: 1.3 “Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.

Rendered redline:
p0045: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or an Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance, including export and migration support, for up to six months after the effective date of expiry or termination at Vendor's then-current rates. Vendor shall not delete Customer Data except in accordance with Sections 11.2 and 11.3.

Comment:
[Playbook] We replaced the immediate cessation of assistance and deletion of Customer Data with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, which our playbook requires and which is also needed for the export and certified-deletion mechanics in Sections 11.2 and 11.3 and the transition period referenced in Section 10.1 to work. If six months is difficult, we can accept ninety days.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and verified 19 findings. Twelve clauses are compliant, several of them meaningfully favourable to us (IP ownership, assignment and change of control, audit, renewal, governing law, insurance, and the express confirmation in § 12.3 that we have given no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment).

Seven items are deviations and, in our view, must be fixed before signature. Two are critical: there is **no Vendor indemnity anywhere in the Agreement** (§ 20 runs one way against us for "every claim"), and the liability cap in § 21.1 is **one month of Fees "actually paid", without exception**, against a USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay commitment. Five further deviations impose one-sided restrictions on us or strip our protections: full-term sole-supplier exclusivity (§ 2.2), a 24-month worldwide post-term non-compete (§ 12.4), a Services licence limited to Customer alone and revocable at Vendor's discretion (§ 13.1), a three-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights (§ 2.1), immediate cessation of assistance and deletion of Customer Data on termination (§ 11.1), and a 15-day Deliverable warranty with an express cut-off of any correction or refund obligation (§ 19.2).

A notable feature of the draft is internal inconsistency: §§ 2.2, 12.4 and 2.1 contradict § 12.3; § 21.1's "without exception" contradicts the Excluded Claims construct in § 21.3; § 11.1 contradicts §§ 11.2–11.3 and § 10.1; and § 9.3 cross-refers to a "Section 20.5" that does not exist. Most of our redlines therefore align the drafting with terms the Vendor has already accepted elsewhere in the document.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | § 20.1 (and broken cross-reference at § 9.3) | No Vendor indemnity at all (no IP, breach of law, data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct), coupled with a one-way Customer indemnity for "every claim" relating to our use of the Services. Walk-away. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 21.1 (cf. §§ 21.2–21.4) | Cap of one month's Fees "actually paid", "without exception", placing indemnities, confidentiality, data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP inside the cap. Below the six-month walk-away threshold. |
| 3 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 (cf. § 12.3) | Full-term sole and exclusive supplier obligation on us, with no category narrowing, 12-month limit or performance exit. Walk-away. |
| 4 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 (cf. § 12.3) | 24-month post-term non-compete, undefined scope, unlimited territory, and bars acquisitions. Walk-away. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 13.1 (cf. §§ 13.2–13.3) | Services licence to Customer alone, expressly excluding Affiliates and contractors, and revocable at Vendor's sole discretion. Walk-away. |
| 6 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Deviation** | § 2.1 (cf. §§ 7.1, 9.4, 12.3) | Three-year USD 2,000,000 p.a. take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights". Walk-away. |
| 7 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Deviation** | § 11.1 (cf. §§ 10.1, 11.2–11.3) | Immediate discontinuation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data, with no export or migration support. Walk-away. |
| 8 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 19.2 (cf. § 6.1, § 19.4) | 15-day conformance warranty from delivery with express cut-off of correction/refund obligations; shorter than the 15-business-day acceptance testing window. |
| 9 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | §§ 14.1–14.4, 13.2, 15.1 | Meets preferred position. Minor sub-preferred points (payment condition on Deliverable ownership; no express "sublicence" wording) noted only. |
| 10 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | §§ 24.1–24.4, 13.3, 9.2 | Meets preferred position in full; § 24.4 blocks Vendor repricing or termination on our change of control. |
| 11 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 9.4 (cf. §§ 7.3, 22.2, 27.3) | No Customer-payable liquidated damages or termination fee; audit shortfall is a compensatory true-up. |
| 12 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9.4 | Preferred position: 30 days' notice, whole or partial, pro-rata refund, no Vendor convenience right during a committed term. |
| 13 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | §§ 22.1–22.3 | Meets preferred position; 5% underpayment cost-shift threshold is better than the fallback, and direct system access is barred. |
| 14 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | §§ 28.1–28.3 | New York law, exclusive New York County courts, no arbitration clause. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 12.3 (cf. §§ 7.1, 8.3) | No MFN or most-favoured-customer burden on us. |
| 16 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 (cf. § 30.1) | No personnel restriction on us; § 12.3 expressly preserves our hiring freedom. |
| 17 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | §§ 8.1–8.3 | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, reminder mechanic, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | §§ 18.1–18.2 | Meets preferred position (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, term plus one year). |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **§ 20 — no Vendor indemnity, one-way Customer indemnity.** We require the Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity, an indemnity procedure and procure/modify/replace/refund IP remedies (new §§ 20.2–20.5, which also cures the broken § 9.3 reference to "Section 20.5"), and narrowing of our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our breach of Applicable Law.
2. **§ 21.1 — one month's Fees, "without exception".** Replace with a mutual cap of the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, expressly subject to the Excluded Claims already set out in § 21.3. §§ 21.2–21.4 can stand.
3. **§ 2.2 — full-term sole-supplier exclusivity.** Make the appointment non-exclusive; § 12.3 stays as drafted.
4. **§ 12.4 — 24-month worldwide non-compete on us.** Delete.
5. **§ 13.1 — Services licence excluding Affiliates/contractors and revocable at Vendor's discretion.** Extend to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf and tie revocation to the notice-and-cure standard already agreed in § 13.3.
6. **§ 2.1 — three-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights.** Replace with pay-for-what-is-ordered-or-used.
7. **§ 11.1 — immediate deletion, no transition support.** Replace with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, subordinated to the data return and certified deletion mechanics in §§ 11.2–11.3.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the eight deviations, with playbook-based comments and the sensible fallbacks flagged in the covering note: a narrowed product/12-month exclusivity or non-compete; a 12-month reducible commitment with true-up in place of take-or-pay; 90 days' transition assistance; and a 90-day (software) / 30-day (services) warranty period.
2. **Escalate items 1 and 2 to the deal owner now.** The absence of any Vendor indemnity and a one-month liability cap are not economically survivable alongside the § 2.1 commitment, and should be raised as gating issues rather than left to a second exchange.
3. **Use the internal contradictions as leverage.** §§ 2.2, 12.4 and 2.1 conflict with § 12.3; § 21.1 conflicts with § 21.3; § 11.1 conflicts with §§ 10.1 and 11.2–11.3; § 9.3 cites a non-existent § 20.5. We should present most of our edits as conforming the draft to positions the Vendor has already accepted.
4. **Ask the Vendor to complete § 23 ("Records and Customer Assurance"),** currently a bare heading, and confirm that no further verification or inspection rights against us are intended — § 22 as drafted is acceptable and we do not want it reopened.
5. **Confirm the warranty/acceptance interlock** so the § 19.2 conformance period runs from acceptance under § 6.1, preserving the § 19.4 remedy.
6. **On close of negotiation,** re-verify that the amended § 21.1 cap, the new §§ 20.2–20.5 and the revised § 11.1 are internally consistent with §§ 9.3, 21.3 and 11.2–11.3 before execution."}

Two are critical: there is **no Vendor indemnity anywhere in the Agreement** (§ 20 runs one way against us for "every claim"), and the liability cap in § 21.1 is **one month of Fees "actually paid", without exception**, against a USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay commitment. Five further deviations impose one-sided restrictions on us or strip our protections: full-term sole-supplier exclusivity (§ 2.2), a 24-month worldwide post-term non-compete (§ 12.4), a Services licence limited to Customer alone and revocable at Vendor's discretion (§ 13.1), a three-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights (§ 2.1), immediate cessation of assistance and deletion of Customer Data on termination (§ 11.1), and a 15-day Deliverable warranty with an express cut-off of any correction or refund obligation (§ 19.2).

A notable feature of the draft is internal inconsistency: §§ 2.2, 12.4 and 2.1 contradict § 12.3; § 21.1's "without exception" contradicts the Excluded Claims construct in § 21.3; § 11.1 contradicts §§ 11.2–11.3 and § 10.1; and § 9.3 cross-refers to a "Section 20.5" that does not exist. Most of our redlines therefore align the drafting with terms the Vendor has already accepted elsewhere in the document.

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **§ 20 — no Vendor indemnity, one-way Customer indemnity.** We require the Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity, an indemnity procedure and procure/modify/replace/refund IP remedies (new §§ 20.2–20.5, which also cures the broken § 9.3 reference to "Section 20.5"), and narrowing of our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our breach of Applicable Law.
2. **§ 21.1 — one month's Fees, "without exception".** Replace with a mutual cap of the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, expressly subject to the Excluded Claims already set out in § 21.3. §§ 21.2–21.4 can stand.
3. **§ 2.2 — full-term sole-supplier exclusivity.** Make the appointment non-exclusive; § 12.3 stays as drafted.
4. **§ 12.4 — 24-month worldwide non-compete on us.** Delete.
5. **§ 13.1 — Services licence excluding Affiliates/contractors and revocable at Vendor's discretion.** Extend to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf and tie revocation to the notice-and-cure standard already agreed in § 13.3.
6. **§ 2.1 — three-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights.** Replace with pay-for-what-is-ordered-or-used.
7. **§ 11.1 — immediate deletion, no transition support.** Replace with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, subordinated to the data return and certified deletion mechanics in §§ 11.2–11.3.
